1.

The claim in this case arises from filing of Dar by the investigating officer of Fir No.575/2017 of
Ps Vivek Vihar regarding receiving of grievous injuries to petitioner/complainant Inderjeet Pandey
in the road side accident.

The accident in question took place on 17.11.2017 at about 01.45 p.m. As
per petitioner/complainant he was going from Kasturba Nagar underpass by driving his motorcycle
bearing no. Dl 5S Bz-8261 and reached red light of Satyam Enclave and was waiting for red light to
turn green.

As the red light turned green, petitioner took right turn towards Vishwas Nagar, in the
meantime one car bearing registration no. Dl 5Ce 1189 being driven by respondent no.1 in a rash
and negligent manner hit the motorcycle of the petitioner/complainant, due to which he fell down
on road and sustained grievous injuries.

Driver of the offending car no. Dl 5Ce 1189 stopped for a
while and thereafter left.

Persons standing near the place of accident informed the registration
number of offending vehicle to injured/complainant.

Injured was immediately taken to Swami
Dayanand Hospital, Dilshad Garden for treatment where Mlc no.4095/17 was prepared.

2. On the complaint of the petitioner Fir No.575/2017 was registered on 17.11.2017 at Ps Vivek
Vihar u/s 279, 338 Ipc.

Io filed the Dar giving details of respondent no.1 being driver and owner of
the offending vehicle which was insured with Oriental Insurance Company being policy
no.211200/31/2018/84268.

Dar was also accompanied with other relevant documents including
Mlc, documents regarding seizure of Dl, insurance company of offending vehicle, insurance policy,
site plan, mechanical inspection report etc.

3.

Respondent no.1 filed WS/reply to the Dar wherein he pleaded that accident has not been caused
by his rash and negligent driving and petitioner got injured due to his own negligence.

4. Respondent no.2/insurance company also filed reply to the Dar stating therein that no cause of
action has arisen.

It is pleaded that accident took place due to entire negligence on the part of
injured/petitioner who was driving his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and on a high
speed.

Insurance company further took the plea of all legal pleas as per the provisions of section
149(2) and 170 of M.V. Act.
5. Predecessor of this court on the basis of material coming on the judicial record, framed following
issues on 20.03.2018 :
(1) Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle bearing no.
Dl5Ce-1189 in rash and negligence manner on 17.11.17 at about 1:45 p.m. at Red
Light towards corner of Shivam Enclave, Vivek Vihar and caused injury to Inderjeet
Pandey?

Opp (2) Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, what amount
and from whom?
Opp (3) Relief.

6. In order to substantiate its case petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. Pw1 himself Inderjeet
Pandey and Pw2 Dr.Dipanker Verma who proved the disability certificate of petitioner wherein it is
mentioned that petitioner suffered 36% of permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.

7. I have heard Sh.S.K. Roy, ld. Counsel for petitioner as well as Sh.Upender Kumar, ld. Counsel for
respondent no.2/insurance company.

I have also gone through the written submissions filed on
behalf of petitioner and insurance company.

Issue No.1
8.

It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the
proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

However, the standard
of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of
preponderance of probabilities.

Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition
based upon negligence.

Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the
Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., Mac App. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 Sc 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) Scr 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law
Suit (Sc) 303.
9.

2017 when he was going somewhere in Kasturba Nagar under pass by driving his motorcycle no.DL 5S BZ 8261 and when he reached red light of Satyam Enclave, upon turning off red light into green, the moment he took right turn towards Vishwas Nagar, offending car bearing registration no.

sentences.text: 2 PW1 due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
PW1 further testifies that he received multiple fractures on his left leg (tibia fibula) and multiple abrasions on other parts of body.
MLC was prepared at Swami Dayanand Hospital.

PW1 in his evidence proved the copy of DAR as Ex.PW1/9.
10.

PW1 was duly cross examined on behalf of respondent no.1/driver cum owner as well as on behalf of respondent no.2/insurance company, however nothing substantive came out in the cross-examination of PW1 regarding rash or negligence on part of the petitioner.

Moreover perusal of site plan of accident also establish that it is when petitioner took right turn towards Vishwas Nagar while coming from Satyam Enclave, car hit the motorcycle of the petitioner in between the road.
Mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle/car no.DL 5CE 1189 also indicate the front bumper, headlight, mud guard of the vehicle have been damaged.

Thus, taking into consideration the entire material placed with DAR and the evidence of PW1, this Tribunal concludes that petitioner has proved that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of R1 in driving of car no.DL 5CE 1189.
Negligence of the petitioner has not been proved at all.
Accordingly issue stands decided.
Issue No.2 11.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,

they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
12.
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
3 possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
5.
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
4 13.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
14.

PW1 in his evidence states that after the accident he was taken to Swami Dayanand Hospital,
Dilshad Garden where his MLC was prepared however most of his treatment was done in Raj Nursing Home and SDN Hospital.

entities.text: Raj Nursing Home and SDN Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW1 proved copy of his discharge card as Ex.PW1/4, medical certificate issued by Raj Nursing Home and Hospital as Ex.PW1/5 and Original medical bills/receipts are collectively Ex.PW1/6.

Discharge card of Raj Nursing Home and Hospital Ex.PW1/4 indicates that petitioner was admitted in that hospital on 17.11.2017 and discharged on 19.11.2017, doctor found multiple fractures on his left leg (tibia fibula) beside other injuries.

Ex.PW1/5 mentions the bill amount of Rs.33,500/- paid by petitioner in Raj Nursing Home &
Hospital.

Beside this petitioner has collectively got exhibited original payments of different bills of treatment as well as pharmacy/chemist including the bill of Raj Nursing Home & Hospital, the total of which is Rs.69,211/-.
On this aspect there is no cross- examination to PW1, nor there is any dispute on behalf of respondents.
As such Rs.69,211/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Loss of earning during treatment:
15.
Petitioner in his evidence testified that because of the accidental injuries he received multiple fractures on his left leg and therefore could not even stand or walk properly for many days.
PW1 says that even at the time of giving evidence he cannot walk properly and feel pain in his injured leg because of the accidental injuries.
PW1 says that he received medical treatment in SDN Hospital and also treated by private doctors.
His treatment is still going on.

At the time of accident petitioner was working as meter reader in Pace Resources Private Limited and was drawing salary of Rs.23,340/-
per month beside other incentives.

PW1 says that he remained on leave from 17.11.2017 to 01.03.2018 because of the accident and therefore lost salary for sum of Rs.81,690/-.
16.

Claimant has claimed loss of income due to accidental injuries for period of four months,
however even in cross-examination PW1 admitted that he has not placed on record any leave record to prove that he remained on leave from 17.11.2017 to 01.03.2018.
As per the medical documents placed on record, petitioner remained hospitalized in Raj Nursing Home and Hospital from 17.11.2017 to 19.11.2017.
Even if it is taken that after his discharge from the hospital petitioner might have taken follow up treatment for recovery.

Still in the absence of any evidence to show that petitioner remained confined to bed and could not join his duties from 17.11.2017 to 01.03.2018 as claimed by him, taking into consideration the multiple fractures suffered by the petitioner and medical documents on record, this Tribunal is of considered view that petitioner is entitled for loss of earning for period of two months.

As such petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.46,680/-
(Rs.23,340 X 2 months) under this head.
Loss of future earning due to disability :

Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
5 17.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."

....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.

13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
6 (i).

entities.text: Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
(iii).
The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
18.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 36% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.

In this regard PW2 Dr. Deepankar Verma, Sr. Resident, Orthopedic, GTB Hospital, Delhi, produced the record relating to disability certificate no. 938/73/08/18 dated 20.08.2018, issued to injured Inderjeet Pandey and proved the same as Ex.PW2/A.

The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
Petitioner was admittedly working with BSES through agency name Pace Resources Private Limited as meter reader.
It came in the evidence of PW1 that because of nature of his job which was essentially a field work for which petitioner had to walk and stand.
Due to the accidental injury his working capacity stated to have affected adversely.

19. PW2 Dr.Deepankar Verma also stated in cross-examination that petitioner had suffered both bone of left leg and further stated that patient can do his daily/routine work without any help, cross leg sitting without any difficulty.
However squatting and walking on stairs with slopes with difficulty.
PW2 states that disablement is permanent in nature, however PW2 states that he cannot comment on disability in respect of whole body.

20. Having considered the entire evidence, medical documents reflect that petitioner suffered multiple fractures on his left leg and his permanent disability to the extent of 36% is also in relation to left lower limb.

In such circumstances when petitioner was admittedly engaged in work of meter reading by visiting different premises for meter reading, he had a field job which involved most of the work by walking and taking stairs etc.
As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 18% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.

Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
7 21.
Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

entities.text: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per photocopy of Aadhar card Ex.PW1/1, PAN Card Ex.PW1/2, DL Ex.PW1/3 and Ex.PW1/7 which is secondary school certificate of CBSE, the age of petitioner as on 17.11.2017 was 45 years 04 months.

As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 13 as applicable to age group between 46-50 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd.,
2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text:
Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd.,
2020 SCC OnLine SC 601
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, considering the petitioner being below 50 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 30%
towards future prospects has to be counted.

22. As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed as Rs.23,340/- + 30%
(Rs.7,002/-), total Rs.30,342/- (Rs.23,340 + Rs.7,002).
Thus applying the functional disability to be 18% of Rs.30,342/-, amount comes out to be Rs.5,461.56.
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.5461.56 X 12 X 13 = Rs.8,52,003/-.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
23.
No evidence has been led by petitioner to prove the fact that any special diet was prescribed or incurring of any conveyance charges.

In the absence of any evidence or prescription of doctor showing prescribing of any special diet, conveyance charges or any evidence to show that any expenditure has been incurred under the above said heading, this Tribunal concludes that petitioner is not entitled for any amount of compensation under the above said heading.

Attendant Charges:
24.
In the absence of any evidence of requirement of keeping any attendant or any expenditure incurred for any attendant.

Though petitioner was given enough opportunity to lead evidence,
however no evidence has been led in this regard so as to warrant this Tribunal to assess attendant charges, if any, incurred by the petitioner for his proper upkeep during the period of his treatment.
As such this Tribunal concludes that petitioner is not entitled for any amount of compensation under the above said heading.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
25.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.

However, compensation Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
8 which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

entities.text: Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
26. In this case, as per MLC of petitioner, he was found to have suffered multiple injuries on his left leg which were opined by the doctor to be grievous in nature.
His treatment record Ex.PW1/4 shows he sustained multiple fractures on his left leg and remained hospitalized from 17.11.2017 to 19.11.2017.
The treatment record further show that even after discharge from the hospital, he had been taking treatment on number of occasions.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.40,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.40,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.

Loss of Amenities:
27.

It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner sustained 36% permanent physical disability in relation to left lower limb, which has been assessed as 18% functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal.
It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned disability,
petitioner
is bound to face difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

28. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1. Medical Expenses Rs.69,211/-
 Loss of earning during Rs.46,680/-
 treatment  Loss of Future Earnings due Rs.8,52,003/-
 to disability  4. Pain & Suffering Rs.40,000/
 5. Loss of Amenities Rs.30,000/
 Total Rs.10,37,894/

9 29.
Thus, the total compensation amount to which the petitioner is entitled comes to Rs.10,37,894/-.
INTEREST ON AWARD 30.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 31.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is an admitted fact that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.2/insurance company.
In view of my findings on above issues, it is held that respondent no.2/ insurance company shall be liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Relief 32.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.10,37,894/- (Rs.Ten Lakh Thirty Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Ninety Four Only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.2/insurance company.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.

The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the award amount in A/c no.20780110171912 (IFSC Code UCBA0002078), UCO Bank, Karkardooma, Delhi, of PO MACT, Shahdara, through RTGS/ NEFT, within 30 days from today.
The respondent no.2 is also directed to give notice regarding deposit of the said amount to the petitioner.
Disbursement of Award Amount 33.

Out of awarded amount, a sum of Rs.1,37,894/- is directed to be released into the saving account of the petitioner and remaining amount of Rs.9,00,000/- along with the interest on the entire award amount is directed to be kept with UCO Bank,
Karkardooma Courts, Delhi in Motor Accident Claims Annuity Deposit (MACAD) in the form FDR (fixed deposit receipt) to be prepared in the name of petitioner for seven years.
The amount of FDR on maturity shall directly be released in petitioner's MACT Saving Bank Account.

The petitioner shall open a saving bank account near the place of his resident.

Further, the bank of petitioner is directed to comply with the following conditions:
(a)The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant i.e., the savings bank account of the claimant shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).

Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
 (i) Whether the disablement is permanent or  temporary;
 (ii) If the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the
proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard
of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of
preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition
based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the
Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., Mac App. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 Sc 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) Scr 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law
Suit (Sc) 303.

The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent Dar- Inderjeet Panday vs Aneesh Nair on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191557923/
3 possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 36% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.
The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
In such circumstances when petitioner was admittedly engaged in work of meter reading by visiting different premises for meter reading, he had a field job which involved most of the work by walking and taking stairs etc.
As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 18% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.

Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].
As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 13 as applicable to age group between 46-50 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Thus, considering the petitioner being below 50 years at the time of accident, an addition of income to the extent of 30%
towards future prospects has to be counted.
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.40,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner sustained 36% permanent physical disability in relation to left lower limb, which has been assessed as 18% functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal.
It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned disability,
is bound to face difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
